subject.title: Feature request: first-class Telegram reaction triggers for agent wake-up and execution

question: Should Telegram reaction control use the shared queue/wake/off notificationWake.reactions policy, a Telegram-specific per-emoji reactionSemantics config, or be deferred until the broader cross-channel reaction-turn contract is settled?
rationale: The remaining work creates public wake/config semantics and overlaps open PRs with different API shapes, so automation should not choose the product contract or open another fix lane.

options.title: Adopt Shared Wake Policy
options.body: Use a shared queue-by-default wake/off policy with stable reaction keys, then repair or land the best candidate with Telegram proof and docs.

options.title: Choose Telegram-Specific Semantics
options.body: Use a Telegram-only reactionSemantics config for mapped emoji actions, accepting a narrower API that may later need cross-channel reconciliation.

options.title: Defer Reaction Execution
options.body: Keep reactions as passive system events for now and close or pause the open implementation PRs until maintainers want this operator-control surface.

recommendation.title: Adopt Shared Wake Policy
recommendation.body: Use a shared queue-by-default wake/off policy with stable reaction keys, then repair or land the best candidate with Telegram proof and docs.

likelyOwner.reason: This person authored the open shared-policy candidate and has recent history in the Telegram reaction, system-event, and plugin boundary paths.
